capabilities: Sync vault files and attachments to a WebDAV-backed repository
Detect and resolve local/remote conflicts, including three-way Markdown merge
Browse commit history, pending changes, and sync logs in a sync center
Probe WebDAV server capabilities and guard remote HEAD updates
Run automatic sync checks on startup, resume, local changes, and polling
disambiguation: It does not mirror the vault as plain files on the remote; remote data lives as immutable blobs and commits in its own repository format.
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been reviewed by Obsidian. Real sync is disabled by default; the plugin starts in planning-only mode and must be explicitly enabled in settings. No screenshots or step-by-step setup guide are included in the README.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to sync a vault to a user's own WebDAV server with conflict detection and history instead of plain file overwriting.
summary: Experimental sync plugin that stores the vault in a WebDAV repository using content-addressed objects, commit snapshots, and a conflict-resolution workspace.
